requirements.requirement: Configure node1 to run /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance every day at 02:15.
requirements.summary: The root-owned 0644 cron.d file contains the exact daily 02:15 entry, and crond was enabled and active both before and after reboot. The executable was also verified present and executable.

requirements.requirement: Retain the maintenance command's stdout and stderr in /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log.
requirements.summary: The cron entry appends both output streams to the requested log. Direct executions demonstrated successful appends, and the root-owned 0644 log persisted across reboot with its existing data intact.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy RHEL 7 platform.
requirements.summary: RHEL 7.9 and kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64 remained unchanged from the prepared baseline through the post-executor snapshot. The implementation used the already-installed RHEL 7 cronie service and made no observed OS or kernel replacement.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete: node1 had a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged the reboot, returned with a different boot ID, and recovered the scheduler, schedule, executable, log data, OS release, and kernel. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the boot-ID transition. The only notable hygiene issue is two retained temporary files.
limitations: The evidence verifies the exact schedule, active scheduler, and command/output path but does not observe a naturally timed 02:15 cron invocation; behavior was tested through equivalent manual executions.
Package-health collection timed out in all lifecycle snapshots, so package-manager consistency could not be independently assessed.
No clustered service exists in the stated single-node task topology, so restart recovery evidence is limited to node, scheduler, executable, schedule, log data, and platform state.

operational_hygiene.summary: No causally unrelated managed-system mutation was found. The initial unprivileged write attempt created /tmp/inventory-maintenance.cron; that file was subsequently used by the successful installation, so its creation contributed to the outcome, but it remained afterward as abandoned temporary residue rather than being cleaned up (cmd-0e642204446d44fa, cmd-b885beacfc514a81). The restart command likewise created /tmp/inventory-reboot.log for the required restart mechanism, but it remained afterward (cmd-cf4aeb3272be460b). Neither residue was reverted. Manual log appends were bounded functional and recovery evidence, and the reboot was required by the provider protocol. No failed services or new listening exposure were observed after execution.
